MY WATER SCIENCE PROJECT

Build a Foil Boat

Shape, test and improve a boat made from one piece of foil. Can you keep its inside dry?

Fold the foil into a wide open boat with raised edges. Place it gently on the water. Observe whether it floats and whether water enters. Dry and reshape the same piece before a second test. Avoid tearing the foil.

With a grown-up: An adult stays beside you throughout water play. Use a shallow plastic tub and objects too large to swallow. Avoid glass, sharp objects and items with batteries. Keep your screen dry and away from the water. Do not drink the water. Dry spills and empty the tub when finished.

Explore before you start.

Open the picture for a closer look, or use the drawing and writing areas below. You can also use paper beside your experiment.

Keep it a fair comparison

Use the same foil and the same tub. Change one feature so you can explain which difference may have helped.

Watch the edges

If an edge dips below the surface, water can enter. A hole can also let water in. Describe what happened before redesigning.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

My first boat

Draw your first design. Show its base and raised edges.

ACTIVITY 2

My improved boat

Change one feature, such as the base width or edge height. Draw the new design.

ACTIVITY 3

What I learned

Compare both designs. What would you try next?

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

A floating boat pushes water aside. Shape affects how much water it can displace before water comes over its edges. A redesign can improve the boat without adding more foil.
